dedupe_keys.name: pakistan floods 2022 post disaster needs assessment water resources and irrigation sector indus basin irrigation system

description: This is the sector chapter of the Pakistan Floods 2022 Post-Disaster Needs Assessment for water resources and irrigation. It describes the Indus Basin Irrigation System, serving over 14 million hectares through three reservoirs, 17 barrages, 12 link canals and 45 canal systems with 58,500 kilometres of canals, plus over 6,000 kilometres of flood dikes. It estimates 2022 flood damage at PKR 152.6 billion, or US$710.6 million, of which flood protection was 36 percent, irrigation channels 32 percent, drainage 14 percent, dams, headworks and weirs 9 percent and supporting infrastructure 8 percent, with 62.2 percent in Sindh, and lists the Lower Swat Canal and Chashma Right Bank Canal among the worst hit. Coverage: national, one flood season, with damage tables by province and recovery needs. Access: a free PDF; reuse is permitted for non-commercial purposes with attribution. Caveats: teams could not visit affected areas, costing methods of provinces were unclear, and losses from suspended irrigation supply are counted under agriculture. It supports flood damage, recovery cost and resilience analysis for irrigation, and relates to the Pakistan monsoon flood extent data record in the catalogue.
